name: Shaking fog harp
subtitle: a fog net whose wires shake off water

effects.effect: wind past a wire sheds swirls from alternate sides and shakes it
a surface of tiny waxy bumps makes drops bead up and roll off

effect: wind past a wire sheds swirls from alternate sides and shakes it
how: Coastal deserts from Chile to Morocco are bathed in fog but short of drinking water, and fog nets lose much of their catch because drops cling to the mesh and blow away or dry. A harp of fine vertical wires with a water-shedding coating catches the fog; the wind itself sheds swirls off each wire and makes it hum and shake, so the beads jump free and slide down into a gutter before they can evaporate.
obstacle: Wires that vibrate for years in salty wind tend to fatigue and snap, and the coating wears off.
why: More water per net in places where fog is the only dependable source.
real: Fog harps with superhydrophobic wires are patented and droplet shedding from vibrated vertical wires is studied, but nothing found using wind-driven vortex-induced vibration to shed drops.
